extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: An open-source dataset for training reasoning models, containing 1.2 million question-answer pairs across math, code, and science domains.
extraction.creator: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, et al.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involves sourcing questions from existing datasets and generating synthetic questions using LLMs, filtering them, deduplicating, and then generating multiple reasoning traces (answers) for each question using a teacher model.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were sourced from a mix of existing datasets, forums, and synthetic generation pipelines, specifically OpenMath-2-Math, CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, StackExchange Physics, and OrganicChemistryPDFs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered by difficulty or response length, deduplicated (exact deduplication for math and science, no deduplication for code), and decontaminated against evaluation benchmarks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations (reasoning traces and answers) were generated by querying a teacher model 16 times per question to elicit distinct responses.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: When sampling multiple responses, multiple aggregation strategies were evaluated to predict the final answer: (1) 'shortest': using the answer of the shortest response; (2) 'longest': using the answer of the longest response; (3) 'majority': using the majority prediction as the final answer. For majority consensus selection, GPT-4o-mini was used to evaluate all responses and return a list of indices of responses that agreed with the majority.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not include data for reinforcement learning. Additionally, supervised fine-tuning on this reasoning data inadvertently degrades the pre-existing safety alignment of models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for training reasoning models.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Our full dataset begins with sourcing many questions in math, code, and science domains. The next step is filtering those questions, deduplicating the math and science questions, randomly sampling questions, and then generating multiple answers for each question.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We can broadly categorize our question sourcing techniques into three types: (1) Fully synthetic – an existing LLM generates questions with little-to-no seed material... (2) Semi-synthetic – an LLM uses existing data sources such as CommonCrawl or FineWeb as seeds to form questions... (3) Non-synthetic – humans write the questions. Examples include StackExchange and ShareGPTCode.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We use OpenMath-2-Math as our sole math question source, CodeGolf and OpenCodeReasoning as our code question sources, and StackExchangePhysics and OrganicChemistryPDFs as our science question sources.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We use difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini for code questions, and response length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini for math and science questions... It uses exact deduplication for math and science and no deduplication for code... We also decontaminate our datasets against our benchmarks by removing samples with high similarity.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Our final pipeline uses 16× answers per question for all domains... We use QwQ-32B as the teacher model.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We use QwQ-32B as the teacher model... We use difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini for code questions, and response length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini for math and science questions.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We did not explore datasets for reinforcement leaming, a standard training regime for building reasoning models... we observe that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning inadvertently degrades the pre-existing safety alignment of Qwen2.5 models... OpenThinker3-7B was trained without any explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data, which likely contributes to its degraded safety performance.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The goal of the OpenThoughts project is to create open-source datasets for training reasoning models... to produce OpenThoughts3-1.2M, and fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on it to yield OpenThinker3-7B.
